issues.description: Field 'numberOfLoopings' in class RollerCoaster has a type mismatch between the UML in the problem statement and the solution implementation. The UML (problem_statement.md lines 26-28) declares RollerCoaster.numberOfLoopings as type int, whereas the solution implementation (src/de/tum/in/ase/RollerCoaster.java) declares the field as long (line 5) and provides getNumberOfLoopings() that returns long (line 12). The constructor in the solution still accepts an int parameter. This inconsistency does not prevent compilation (int can be assigned to long) but will confuse students about the expected attribute type and the getter's return type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute type consistent with the UML. Change the field declaration in src/de/tum/in/ase/RollerCoaster.java from 'private long numberOfLoopings;' to 'private int numberOfLoopings;' and update getNumberOfLoopings() to return int. Alternatively, if long was intended, update the UML/problem statement to declare numberOfLoopings as long. Prefer adjusting the implementation to int to match the UML and the constructor parameter.
